expectations.text: States plainly that the not-empty check is insufficient
expectations.evidence: No. Your new test would have passed on all 21 days of the incident. Non-empty is a check that cannot fail in the failure mode you actually had.

expectations.text: Identifies the COALESCE to zero as the mechanism that made the failure silent
expectations.evidence: The defect isn't the rename. It's COALESCE(x, 0). A null is a signal that the join failed; coalescing converts that signal into a plausible business number. Same shape as except: pass.

expectations.text: Recommends reconciliation against a source of truth, not only shape checks
expectations.evidence: Does it agree? (reconciliation) Yes — warehouse revenue total vs. the source system. #2 Reconcile to source.

expectations.text: Recommends that assertions run before publication rather than after, so bad data cannot reach the dashboard
expectations.evidence: #4 Move the assertion before publication. Build to staging → test staging → promote on pass. If tests run after publish and email a failure, bad data still reached finance.

expectations.text: Recommends a data contract or schema check so an upstream rename fails loudly and attributably
expectations.evidence: #3 Schema contract at ingest. Assert the expected columns exist with expected types before the join runs. A rename is a drop plus an add; it should break loudly.

expectations.text: Recommends volume or null-rate assertions rather than only a non-empty check
expectations.evidence: #1 assert null_rate(revenue_raw) < threshold on the pre-coalesce column. #5 Distribution, not just presence. Revenue vs. trailing same-weekday median.

expectations.text: Treats three weeks of nobody noticing as a detection gap worth its own fix
expectations.evidence: Detection lag is its own finding. What caught this was a human at close — that's not a device, that's luck with a three-week latency.
